class.name: RockField3D
class.brief_description: Places rocks and stones over a [TerrainGenerator3D] by the processes that put them there, in the rock type of each place.
class.description: Six layers, each streamed in square cells round [member follow_target] (or the camera) out to its radius: rockfall blocks from [code skip-lint]TerrainGenerator3D.get_boulders()[/code], scree packed on the talus aprons, glacial boulders and erratics in the till, river cobbles sized by what the flow can move and rounded by the distance travelled, shingle and boulders on lake and sea shores, and jointed blocks set into cliffs in courses along the beds. Stones of a cover are dropped one at a time and rest on those already down (sequential deposition). Shapes come from [RockGenerator], a few variants per rock type and family, shared by every stone as MultiMesh instances. See docs/ideas/rocks.md.

method.name: break_stone
method.description: Breaks the stone whose surface lies nearest [param position], within [param radius]. The stone is hidden and its collision is turned off. In its place goes a [PhysXDestructible3D] of the shape's pieces (see [member RockGenerator.fracture_pieces]), drawn with a copy of the rock material that carries the stone's own instance data, and [param damage] is applied at [param position] over [param radius]. The bottom pieces, sunk in the ground (or held in a wall or a tor), stay put; the rest fall. The stone stays broken when its cell is rebuilt, until [method restore_broken]. A shape is fractured once and shared by every stone of that shape. Shapes near the follow target are fractured ahead (see [member break_prepare_radius]); otherwise the first hit builds it. Returns the new node, or [code]null[/code] if no stone is in reach or the godot_physx module is missing (see [method is_breaking_supported]).

method.name: build_area
method.description: Builds every layer in [param rect] (x and z) now, ignoring [member build_budget_msec]. Returns the number of cells built.

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes every stone.

method.name: get_broken_count
method.description: How many stones [method break_stone] has broken since the last [method restore_broken] or [method rebuild].

method.name: get_cell_count
method.description: Cells built.

method.name: get_close_up_shape_count
method.description: Number of close-up shapes loaded (built and kept within [member close_up_max_shapes]).

method.name: get_close_up_triangle_count
method.description: Triangles in the loaded close-up shapes.

method.name: get_coarse_cover_at
method.description: This field's answer to [method WorldGround.coarse_cover_at]: pebble, gravel and fine shares of the ground (0..1) from the cover maps, bilinear; the near map where it reaches, else the far one; 0 outside both or with [member ground_detail_cover] off.

method.name: get_far_cover_texture
method.description: The far cover map the terrain reads as [code]rock_far_cover_map[/code]: 256 x 256 texels of 32 m centred on the target, rgb the stones' weathered colour, alpha their plan cover (rockfall blocks, glacial boulders on till and coarse river beds). Null while [member far_radius] is 0.

method.name: get_frost_at
method.description: The frost sorting at a world position: x is how strongly the ground there sorts (0 to 1, from the climate, wetness, slope, soil and water gates of [member frost_sorting]), y the stone share of the pattern there (1 on a stony border or stripe, 0 in a fine centre). (0, 0) with [member frost_sorting] off or no [WeatherMap3D].

method.name: get_pedestal_at
method.description: Rain splash pedestals at a world position: x is the share of the ground's stones lying on bare, erodible soil there (0 to 1: bare from a dry climate or a recent burn, times the soil, slope and stoniness gates of [member rain_pedestals]), y the soil the rain has taken off round them in metres. y is 0 with [member rain_pedestals] off, (0, 0) with no climate.

method.name: get_ground_detail_count
method.description: Ground detail stones built in [param layer] (one of the LAYER_DETAIL constants), or in all three with -1.

method.name: get_cells_pending
method.description: Coarse cells being placed on worker threads (see [member cell_threads]), and shape libraries being built for them.

method.name: get_ground_detail_cover_rect
method.description: The world XZ rectangle the cover map of [param level] (0 near, 1 far) covers as built, empty before it is built. See [method get_ground_detail_cover_texture].

method.name: get_ground_detail_cover_texture
method.description: The ground detail cover map at [param level] (0: 1 m texels, 1: 8 m texels; see [member ground_detail_cover]): red, green and blue hold the pebbles', gravel's and fine gravel's share of the ground (0 to 0.5 as 0 to 255), alpha the rock type times 32. [code]null[/code] until built.

method.name: get_ground_detail_pending
method.description: Ground detail cells being placed on worker threads (see [member ground_detail_threads]).

method.name: get_ground_detail_tile_stats
method.description: [member ground_detail_tiles] so far: [code]tiles[/code] cut, [code]placements[/code] and the [code]grains[/code] they draw (since the field was made); [code]live_placements[/code], [code]live_grains[/code], [code]instances[/code] (rendering instances, one per shape of a placement) and [code]tile_triangles[/code] now; the shared sets now ([code]shared_sets[/code], their [code]shared_candidates[/code], the [code]shared_tiles[/code] some placement took and their [code]shared_triangles[/code], and [code]shared_by_class[/code]: sets, candidates, taken and triangles for pebble, gravel and fine); and the squares looked at and why some were left as single grains ([code]skip_sparse[/code], [code]skip_coarse[/code], [code]skip_bent[/code], [code]skip_unmatched[/code]). Also the far thinning now: [code]far_thinned_groups[/code], [code]far_widened_groups[/code] and their [code]far_widen_mean[/code] ([member far_widen]).

method.name: get_last_build_msec
method.description: Milliseconds the last build step took.

method.name: get_last_detail_msec
method.description: The main thread's share of the ground detail in the last streaming update, in milliseconds: snapshots for the workers and adding their finished cells.

method.name: get_last_library_msec
method.description: Milliseconds spent building shape libraries in the last build step.

method.name: get_layer_density
method.description: Density of a layer.

method.name: get_layer_radius
method.description: Radius round the follow target out to which a layer is built.

method.name: get_library_triangle_count
method.description: Triangles in the most detailed level of every shape built so far.

method.name: get_contact_texture
method.description: The ground contact map (see [member ground_contact]): 64 m a side at 1024 texels round the follow target, red the damp ring round each stone's foot, green the fines banked against its uphill side. Published as the [code]rock_contact_map[/code] and [code]rock_contact_rect[/code] shader globals, which [TerrainMaterial3D] reads.

method.name: get_last_contact_usec
method.description: Microseconds the last contact map took to draw on its worker thread.

method.name: get_moss_pending
method.description: Moss shells still building on worker threads (see [member moss_cushions]).

method.name: get_moss_shell_count
method.description: Moss shells drawn on the close-up stones now (see [member moss_cushions]).

method.name: get_moss_triangle_count
method.description: Triangles in the moss shells drawn now.

method.name: get_obstacles
method.description: Stones in [param rect] of b-axis diameter at least [param min_size], as [code](x, ground y, z, footprint radius)[/code], for vegetation obstacles and water flow. Placement is deterministic, so this works for cells not built yet. Each placement cell is placed once and kept (16 bytes a stone) until [method rebuild], so repeated and overlapping queries are fast. Cliff blocks are left out.

method.name: get_loose_count
method.description: How many stones are rigid bodies now (see [member stones_react]).

method.name: get_rt_stats
method.description: What the cells' stones cost the path tracer now: [code]merged_triangles[/code], [code]merged_groups[/code] and [code]merged_stones[/code] (groups at or under [member ProjectSettings.rendering/pathtracing/multimesh_merged_blas_max_triangles], whose merged structure holds a copy of each stone's triangles), [code]instanced_groups[/code] and [code]instanced_stones[/code] (sharing their shape's structure), and [code]cell_triangles[/code], every cell stone's triangles. See [member rt_instanced_cells].

method.name: get_react_stats
method.description: [member stones_react] so far: [code]loose[/code] (rigid bodies now), [code]promoted[/code], [code]pressed[/code] (into the ground under the footprint), [code]shoved[/code] (out to its rim) and [code]settled[/code] (counts since the field was made).

method.name: get_rockfall_dust_impacts
method.description: How many impacts of falling or broken pieces have thrown up dust since the field entered the tree.

method.name: get_rockfall_dust_node
method.description: The [PhysXRockDust3D] the field made for its rockfall dust, or [code]null[/code] when [member rockfall_dust] is off or the engine was built without NVIDIA Flow.

method.name: get_rockfall_dust_total
method.description: Kilograms of fines the field's falling and broken stones have thrown up since it entered the tree.

method.name: get_rockfall_trigger
method.description: How many times [member live_rockfall_rate] the falls come now, from the active [WeatherMap3D] at the follow target's height (air cooled 6.5 C per km above the weather's ground height): 1, plus 3 in the frost-cracking window (-8 to -3 C), plus 6 for two game hours after the air thaws through 0 C, plus the rain rate in mm/h over 5. 1 without weather.

method.name: get_stone_caps
method.description: Like [method get_stones], with each stone's cap, where moss, snow and litter settle, from its base shape: the largest connected patch of up-facing surface (normals within about 45 degrees of up), not the region round the highest point. [code]cap_point[/code] (Vector3, the patch's centre on the surface), [code]cap_normal[/code] (Vector3, its mean normal) and [code]cap_radius[/code] (metres out from the centre that the surface stays within [param tolerance] metres of the cap's plane). No physics is needed. The base shape is used, so the close-up shapes' millimetre relief does not shrink the caps.

method.name: get_stone_count
method.description: Stones built.

method.name: get_stones
method.description: Stones of a layer in [param rect], placed whether or not they are built, as dictionaries with [code]position[/code], [code]basis[/code], [code]scale[/code], [code]ground[/code], [code]footprint[/code], [code]film[/code], [code skip-lint]rock_type[/code], [code]family[/code], [code]bin[/code], [code]variant[/code], [code skip-lint]layer[/code] and [code]top[/code] (height of its highest point, from its shape as placed).

method.name: get_wind_obstacles
method.description: Boulders in [param rect] standing at least 0.5 m out of the ground, as world [AABB]s (the footprint's square, from the ground to about the stone's top). The weather's shelter reads them (the field joins the [code]weather_shelter[/code] group), so snow drifts and blown sand settle in their lee. Empty while [member wind_obstacles] is off.

method.name: is_breaking_supported
method.description: Whether [method break_stone] can work: the engine has the godot_physx module, with [PhysXDestructible3D] and [PhysXBlastAuthoring].

method.name: is_layer_enabled
method.description: Whether a layer is placed.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Removes every stone and builds again round the follow target.

method.name: restore_broken
method.description: Frees the broken stones' pieces and puts every broken stone back. The cells are built again.

method.name: set_layer_density
method.description: Scales how many stones a layer places.

method.name: set_layer_enabled
method.description: Turns a layer on or off.

method.name: set_layer_radius
method.description: Sets how far round the follow target a layer is built.

method.name: trigger_rockfall
method.description: Looses a random built cliff block within [param radius] of [param position] now, as [member live_rockfall] does, and returns its [PhysXDestructible3D] (null if there is none, or without the godot_physx module). Its fracture is built at once if it is not ready, which can take tens of milliseconds, so call it sparingly.

method.name: write_terrain3d_holes
method.description: Writes every cave hole of the generator (see [method TerrainGenerator3D.add_hole]) into the [member terrain3d] node's control map, for a Terrain3D set after the caves were placed. Returns how many holes.

members.member: Density of the stone for the mass of a broken stone, in kg/m³. Quartz-feldspar rock is about 2650.
How many pieces each shape breaks into. See [member RockGenerator.fracture_pieces].

Shapes of the stones with collision within this distance of the follow target are fractured ahead on a worker thread, one at a time, so that a hit breaks them at once. 0 turns this off, and each shape is then fractured at its first hit.
Milliseconds per frame spent building cells while streaming.

While streaming, the cells of the coarse layers (field stones, scree, river and shore stones, landforms) are placed on worker threads, and the main thread only adds their MultiMeshes and collision. A cell whose shapes are not built yet starts them on workers and is placed again once they are in. Landform cells stay on the main thread while [member cave_mouths] is on, as those open terrain holes. Off: placed on the main thread within [member build_budget_msec], as before.
Scales how many blocks are set into cliff faces.
Jointed blocks set into steep bare faces in courses along the beds.
How far round the follow target cliff blocks are built.

Near the follow target, stones are drawn with close-up shapes: the same stone on a grid of about 3 mm cells carrying the rock's millimetre fabric as geometry (crystals, grains, laminae, karren, vesicles, cleavage steps, conchoidal ripples). Built on worker threads as they are first wanted. Not used for cobbles and pebbles, whose base shapes already hold it.
Close-up shapes kept loaded; beyond this, the ones no stone has wanted for 30 seconds are dropped.
Distance in metres from the follow target to a stone's surface within which it is drawn with its close-up shape.
Scales how often a cliffed coast gets a sea stack or arch (at most one per 128 m cell).
Sea stacks and arches of jointed wall blocks standing off cliffed coasts, with fallen blocks at their feet and a jointed rock platform at the cliff foot just above the water line.
How far round the follow target sea stacks, arches and platforms are built.

The landform layer stands a cave mouth (RockGenerator [code]FAMILY_CAVE_MOUTH[/code]: a limestone outcrop with a passage opening into it, fallen blocks at its entrance) at the foot of some bare limestone cliffs. The block is set into the face, leaning back with it up to 25 degrees, and its passage opens through the ground: it adds a hole to the [member generator] ([method TerrainGenerator3D.add_hole]) that [Landscape3D] leaves out of its mesh and collision (and a [member terrain3d] out of its control map), and stones of the other layers are not placed in it. The block takes the colour of the landscape's rock layer ([member ground_material]). Off by default: on walls gentler than the block's lean its outline stands out of the slope.

Coast forms (stacks, arches, platforms) get collision at any distance, whatever [member collision_enabled] says, so a sea measuring its floor by ray casts (PhysXWaterSurface3D seabed_from_floor) sees them as shore: foam, run-up and wave bending round them. The field asks the generator's sea to remeasure its floor after building coast forms.
Gives stones near the follow target convex hull collision shapes, one static body per cell.
Physics layers of the stone collision bodies.
Smallest b-axis diameter that gets collision.
How far round the follow target stones get collision.
Scales the grid resolution of every shape. Lower builds faster and coarser.
Scales how many ground detail fine gravel are placed.
Ground detail fine gravel, while [member ground_detail] is on.
How far from the camera the ground detail fine gravel reach. Set from the camera while [member ground_detail] is on (see [member ground_detail_pixels]).
Scales how many ground detail gravel are placed.
Ground detail gravel, while [member ground_detail] is on.
How far from the camera the ground detail gravel reach. Set from the camera while [member ground_detail] is on (see [member ground_detail_pixels]).
Scales how many ground detail pebbles are placed.
Ground detail pebbles, while [member ground_detail] is on.
How far from the camera the ground detail pebbles reach. Set from the camera while [member ground_detail] is on (see [member ground_detail_pixels]).
Rock type of glacial erratics, carried from elsewhere.

The path tracer draws the cells' stones as instances of their shapes (one shared acceleration structure per shape, one entry per stone) instead of a merged structure per group that holds a copy of every stone's triangles. The same image; less memory only where many groups would be merged (where most are already over the cap, the CPU copies of the records cost more than the merged copies saved), and more instances to trace. See [method get_rt_stats].

While [member far_thinning] thins a cell, the stones it still draws grow (up to 1.6 times) so the field keeps the stone cover of the records it dropped, as the ground's far stones take over. The far tier's big stones are never widened, so they meet their far copies.
Node the layers stream round. Empty uses the current camera.
The [TerrainGenerator3D] whose height, slope, talus, till, rivers, cliffs and water levels place the stones.
Scales how many glacial boulders are placed.
Subrounded boulders and erratics on the till and the ground a glacier left.
How far round the follow target glacial boulders are built.

Eases each stone's foot into the ground under it: over a band of [member ground_blend_height] the stone takes the ground layer's colour and roughness (the hollows first, the proud parts last, with a thinning dust above) and its normal turns toward the ground's, following the slope under the stone. The layer comes from the generator's geology, coloured as [member ground_material]'s layers, with its grain (fines and pale and dark chips). The lowest part is damp (darker, smoother), and the band rises on the uphill side, where debris banks up. See also [member ground_contact].
The ground-blend band's height in metres for a 1 m stone; it grows with the square root of the stone's size.

The ground side of a stone's contact. Soil beside a stone stays damper (stones act as a mulch), so it is darker and smoother, and the fines washed downhill bank up against the stone's uphill side. The field draws both into a map round the follow target on a worker thread, and [TerrainMaterial3D] darkens and tints the ground by it. The map is redrawn when the target moves 8 m or the field is rebuilt. With [member ground_blend], which paints the stone's own foot, the stone reads as sitting in the ground.

The stones under [member min_size] near the camera as real instanced geometry instead of the ground material's normal map, so they have silhouettes, contact shadows and parallax under raster and the path tracer alike. Three size classes (1 to 2 cm, 2 to 4 cm, 4 cm to [member min_size]) continue the shore's and the talus's own size laws, so they keep the big stones' sorting and rock; each class is drawn round the camera out to where its stones are still [member ground_detail_pixels] tall, and every stone shares one of the field's shapes, so the path tracer only adds an instance for each (see [method RenderingServer.multimesh_set_rt_instanced]). Cells are placed on worker threads while streaming (see [member ground_detail_threads]). Turn it off in tests that do not need it. The grains rest on the drawn ground: the heightfield plus [method WorldGround.relief_at] (the landscape's cliff and bank relief); [signal WorldGround.relief_changed] lays the cells over the change again.

Past where each ground detail class stops drawing its stones, the ground material shows their aggregate instead: how much of the ground they cover, their colour, the bed they hide when seen edge on and the shade they cast under a low sun, so the edge of the drawn stones never shows. The cover comes from the same size and density laws as the stones, in two maps round the camera (1 m texels over 256 m and 8 m texels over 2 km, see [method get_ground_detail_cover_texture]) built on worker threads as it moves. Needs a [TerrainMaterial3D] ground and [member ground_detail] on.

Ground detail on the river beds: the river layer's bed carried on below [member min_size] (what the flow can move and what still arrives from upstream), coarse in the riffles and fine in the pools between them about six channel widths apart, finer on the bars at the sides, the pools' beds partly hidden under a drape of fines, and every grain imbricated (its long axis across the flow, dipping upstream 10 to 30 degrees). Most grains carry the rock of the river's headwaters. Off, the beds keep only the river layer's stones.

The ground detail follows the game trails and the boar rooting [WorldStand] publishes: a trail's tread keeps an armour of angular stones standing proud while its gravel and fines thin out and gather on its shoulders, and a fresh rooting leaves stones turned up loose on the soil, settling over two years. [signal WorldStand.stand_changed] builds the detail cells over the change again.

Gravel sorted by storm runoff in the ground detail: the floors of the terrain's rills and gullies ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_gully_at], the same rule the terrain material draws their gravel by) keep a lag of the coarse grains, a little rounded and imbricated across the flow, their gravel and fines washed out; the fans below them, where the slope eases, take a spread of fine grains over the coarser ground. Tiles of piles are not cut over a channel or fan.

Rain splash pedestals in the ground detail: where plants leave the soil bare (a dry climate from the [WorldContracts] weather's yearly precipitation times the terrain's precipitation pattern, or a burn scar from [WorldFire] in its first years), stones of the soil lie on it, and each stands on a column of the soil it shielded from the raindrops' splash while the ground round it was lowered (up to about a third of the stone's width); some have toppled off theirs. Trails, rooting, frost churn and storm runoff level them. Drawn as soil columns of fresh subsoil under the stones; counted in the far cover map. Tiles of piles are not cut over them. Off, the same stones lie on the soil without their columns.

Frost-sorted patterned ground in the ground detail: where the mean annual air from the active [WeatherMap3D] climate (cooled by its lapse rate with height) is below about -1 C, the year's precipitation is over about 300 mm, the ground slopes under 10 degrees and has soil over bare rock, away from water, sand and talus, freeze and thaw sort the stones from the fines. Flat ground shows circles 1 to 3 m across, stony borders round bare fine centres; from 2 to 5 degrees the borders draw out into stripes down the fall line. The pattern comes from a phase separation run once per kind (Cahn-Hilliard, after Kessler and Werner 2003), tiled with warp and rotation per block so it does not repeat. The border stones are blocky and coarse, piled over the soil, some heaved up on edge. Tiles of piles are not used where the pattern is. Past the drawn stones the far cover maps ([member ground_detail_cover]) carry the borders' stones by the pattern's mean share. The gate and stone share are also published round the target as the global terrain_frost_map (r gate, g stone share, b dome) over terrain_frost_rect, so [TerrainMaterial3D] shades the fine centres as bare wet silt domed by frost heave (b: the dome's height share) and the borders with a gravel lag. See [method get_frost_at].

Tiles of piles: each ground detail cell is cut into 4 x 4 squares, and squares on near-flat ground, clear of coarse stones, are drawn as placements of tiles. The tiles are shared by every cell of a block of 16 x 16 cells: sampled squares spread over the block, placed on their own, so a block's tiles are the same whatever order its cells stream in. A square takes a tile only where it matches its grain count, size, rock shares and wetness within what a square varies by chance, chosen by its hash from its first two matches, never a neighbour's, turned a random quarter turn. A square with no shared match takes one of up to four tiles cut from its own cell's grains. A shared tile is built from its third placement on: the first two draw as their single grains, since a tile used once or twice costs more ray tracing memory than the grains it replaces. Each shape of a tile is one [MultiMesh] whose merged ray tracing BLAS every placement shares, so one placement costs a few ray tracing instances instead of one per grain. Grains resting on coarser grains stay single. A contact splits the placement under it back into single grains so they react. The ground blend of a tile's grains uses the placement's plane (the rock shader's [code]rock_tile_plane[/code]).

While streaming, place the ground detail cells on worker threads: the main thread only snapshots what a cell rests on and adds the finished cell, one buffer upload a shape. A finer size class waits until the coarser ones round it are down. When disabled, each cell is placed on the main thread as it is wanted.
The most stones one ground detail cell (2, 4 or 8 m square) holds.
The farthest any ground detail class reaches from the camera.
How tall, in pixels, a ground detail class's mean stone is at the edge of its reach.
The image height the ground detail's reach is worked out for; 0 uses the viewport's own.

Overrides the material the ground blend takes its colours from: each layer's colour times the mean of its albedo texture. When unset, the field uses the [TerrainMaterial3D] of the [Landscape3D] that draws its generator (else any landscape's), so the blend matches the ground with no wiring; with no landscape either, the terrain material's default colours.
Scales how many landforms are placed.
Bedrock landforms where their rock and setting are: limestone pavement (clints and grykes) on flat, bare limestone, and rows of hoodoos on steep, bare, soft bedded rock.
How far round the follow target landforms are built.

Caprock slabs along the lips of the terrain's benches ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_ledge_lips]): one slab between two cross joints after another, each as thick as the lip's cap, hanging out by its overhang, its back under the bench; a gap now and then where a block fell.
Lichen crust on upper faces, from 0 to 1.

Cliff blocks near the follow target come loose now and then and fall as [PhysXDestructible3D] bodies that break on hard impacts and stay as debris. The falls follow a Poisson process at [member live_rockfall_rate] times [method get_rockfall_trigger]: more in frost and thaw and in heavy rain. A block's fracture is built on a worker first, so a fall does not stall the frame. Needs the godot_physx module and the cliff layer. The signal [signal rockfall] reports each fall.
Falls kept; past this the oldest fall's pieces are freed.
How far from the follow target blocks fall, in metres. None fall within 20 m of it unless [method trigger_rockfall] is called.
Falls per game hour (in the [WeatherMap3D] time scale) within [member live_rockfall_radius], before the weather's trigger factor.
Caps the stones of one cell of one layer.

Glossy crystals smaller than a pixel still flash: quartz and feldspar cleavage on granite, quartz and mica grains on the other rocks, counted per cell of the pixel's footprint in raster and the exact crystal's facet under the path tracer. Lichen, moss, a water film, snow and the ground's dust cover them; the weathered rind dulls them.
Smallest b-axis diameter placed in metres. Smaller stones stay in the terrain material.
Moss on upper, shaded and wet faces, from 0 to 1.

Moss as real geometry on the close-up stones (within [member close_up_radius], 30 cm and bigger). Each stone gets a shell lifted off its close-up shape where the rock shader paints moss: on tops, in hollows, on the pole-facing side and near damp ground, with the same noise. The shell is about 1 cm deep as a mat and up to 3.5 cm as a cushion, lumpy, with a ragged margin sunk into the rock. Its material draws the moss shoots a few millimetres across. The shells are built on worker threads and kept while the stone stays close. Off, the moss is the shader's tint only.
Scales how many river stones are placed.
Cobbles in river beds, sized by what the flow can move and fining downstream, rounded by the distance travelled and imbricated against the current.
Smallest drainage area in square metres whose river gets stones.
How far round the follow target river stones are built.
The main rock of the terrain.
Scales how many rockfall blocks are placed.
With [member stones_react]: how many stones may be rigid bodies at once; past it the stones a body touches are shoved aside instead.

Dust where falling and broken stones hit, break and slide: the kinetic energy an impact takes out of a piece times [member rockfall_dust_per_joule], a little from each new fracture face, and a trickle from pieces sliding or rolling on the ground, less in rain. The field makes its own [PhysXRockDust3D] to carry it in NVIDIA Flow when the engine has Flow.
Kilograms of airborne fines per joule of kinetic energy an impact takes out of a piece.
Blocks fallen from cliffs where [code skip-lint]TerrainGenerator3D.get_boulders()[/code] puts them.
How far round the follow target rockfall blocks are built.
Scales how many scree stones are placed.
Stones packed on talus aprons, sorted by size down the slope.
How far round the follow target scree is built.
Seed of the placement and the shapes.
Scales how many shore stones are placed.
Shingle and boulders on lake and sea shores, sized by beach slope.
How far round the follow target shore stones are built.
Rock type of the soft beds when [member use_strata] is on.

Small stones react to whatever stands, walks or drives on them: every node in the [code]world_contact[/code] group (read with [method WorldContracts.describe_body]). Of the stones under its footprint that have no collision of their own, most are pressed flat into the ground (into the print a deformable ground took), some are shoved out to the footprint's rim, and a few become rigid bodies for a moment, flicked on with a share of its speed (up to [member react_max_bodies] at a time, from 1.2 cm across), going back to plain instances where they come to rest. A loose stone stays in its own [MultiMesh] the whole time, so raster and the path tracer draw it unchanged. Boulders (over 0.3 m) never move. See [method get_react_stats].
Builds and frees cells round the follow target as it moves, within [member build_budget_msec] a frame.

An optional Terrain3D node (the addon, used by name, so the engine builds without it) whose heights come from the [member generator]. Each cave mouth's hole is also written into its control map ([code]Terrain3DData.set_control_hole[/code] on every vertex whose ground lies in the passage, then [code]update_maps[/code] and its collision update), so the cave opens on a Terrain3D ground as it does on a [Landscape3D].
Scales how often a crest gets a tor or an outcrop.

Tors on the most convex crests of thin soil: stacks of corestones ([constant RockGenerator.FAMILY_CORESTONE]) two to five tiers high, most on granite, fewer on sandstone and basalt, plus low outcrops of one tier on other crests.
How far round the follow target tors and outcrops are built.
Uses [member soft_rock_type] where the terrain strata are soft.
Shapes per rock type and family. Every stone uses one of them as a MultiMesh instance.

Boulders block the wind: the field joins the [code]weather_shelter[/code] group and gives its boulders through [method get_wind_obstacles], so WeatherMap3D slows the wind in their lee and snow and sand drift there.

signal.name: rockfall
signal.description: A cliff block came loose at [param position] (out of the face), of [param mass] kg. For sound and camera shake.

constants.constant: Sea stacks, arches and wave-cut platforms on cliffed coasts.

Bedrock landforms: limestone pavement on flat bare limestone, hoodoo rows on steep bare soft rock, and rows of sandstone fins (some holed by arches) on gentle bare sandstone, clusters of goblins on flat bare sandstone, pothole slabs with grinder stones in steep bedrock stream beds and, with [member cave_mouths], cave mouths at limestone cliff feet.
Ground detail: pebbles from 4 cm to [member min_size] (on talus, to the scree layer's own smallest), placed only while [member ground_detail] is on.
Ground detail: gravel of 2 to 4 cm, placed only while [member ground_detail] is on.
Ground detail: fine gravel of 1 to 2 cm, placed only while [member ground_detail] is on.
